company.html.text: (( • )) ROGERAI · company An American AI research and infrastructure company. RogerAI builds local-first inference infrastructure and open models for the hardware people and plants already own. We are based in Orange County, California. Our roadmap answers to the machines it runs on rather than to a growth curve. What we build Join us Broadcasts FAQ Let’s talk THE PRODUCT The RogerAI network routes work to models running on real hardware - the frontier, decentralized. THE LAB RogerAI Labs builds the open edge models and publishes the weights. Each half makes the other worth more: a model you own is more useful when there is somewhere to run it and earn from it, and the network is more useful the better small models get. Running a RogerAI model locally never requires the network, and the network is not restricted to RogerAI models. §1 / WHAT WE BUILD Two lines of work, one engineering discipline. One line is a network that sends real work to machines other people own. The other is a family of small models built for the hardware those machines actually have. PRODUCT SHIPPING The RogerAI network An OpenAI-compatible endpoint over models running across community and private hardware. It handles discovery, capacity-aware routing, failover, metering, and signed receipts, while the operator keeps physical control of the machine and opens no inbound ports. Available as a CLI, an OpenAI-compatible API, and an iOS app. Evaluate Live models · Manual Source github.com/rogerai-fyi/roger RESEARCH ACTIVE RogerAI Labs Open model and inference research for edge, embedded, and industrial use: quantization, pruning, runtime work, and the Wave family of device-first small models. Results ship with the hardware they ran on, the harness that ran them, and the raw outputs, so anyone can rerun them. Programs Research notebook Evidence Open Air Waves Weights huggingface.co/rogerai-fyi POSITION Frontier capability, local footprint Two directions, one goal: make frontier-capability models reachable on hardware you control, and make small models good enough that the frontier is not always the answer. Optimization work brings large open models down to workstation class; the Wave program builds up from the single machine at the edge. Our models ship in open formats on standard runtimes, so nothing we publish depends on RogerAI continuing to exist. §2 / FOCUS The smallest model that can do the job. We build for embedded and edge systems where operational-technology networks are segmented or air-gapped and data cannot leave. A right-sized family. The Wave Spectrum runs pico to exa on one SI scale. Every tier is named for where it sits. Wave Pico reads a single machine’s telemetry on hardware beside it. Wave Nano concentrates a fleet at the gateway. Wave Micro reasons across a facility, Wave Giga across a plant, and Wave Tera across many plants at once. Wave Peta carries regional scale, carved down from Wave Exa. Exa is the frontier flagship, and the teacher the rest of the family learns from. Every tier ships with Wave Mesh baked in, and understands the output of every tier beneath it. Industrial deployment. Our focus spans oil and gas, power generation, manufacturing, aerospace, mining, water, healthcare, and defense sustainment: advisory workloads beside existing control systems, never replacing deterministic protection or safety paths. In healthcare that means the equipment and facilities layer - never diagnosis, treatment, or a patient’s care. Evidence before claims. Measurements name the hardware, evaluation harness, settings, and raw results. Our models use open formats and standard runtimes. Local inference sends no telemetry. Negative results remain visible. See the research notebook for programs, industry use cases, constraints, and device evidence. §3 / ORIGIN & OPENNESS Built here. Useful anywhere. RogerAI is built in Orange County, California. “American-made” describes the company, product engineering, and RogerAI-authored research, built on upstream open models and a global research community. Open where the component is open. Our open-source model and runtime work, recipes, converters, evaluations, and qualifying weights are published with their actual licenses and lineage. Source-visible is not the same claim. The RogerAI network and broker are licensed under PolyForm Perimeter 1.0.0, and the node-agent protocol and usage-receipt SDK are Apache 2.0 so anyone can implement them. We publish the source, but do not call the platform open source. Each model carries its own license rather than borrowing a broader marketing label. Model license. A released Wave model will carry its own license, and may be used locally without the network. Optional broker publication, routing, payments, failover, and receipts are network services governed by separate network terms. Those terms do not modify the model license. §4 / CONTACT Talk to the people building it. RogerAI is operated by RogerAI, Inc., a Delaware corporation , from Orange County, California. The Terms carry the contracting details. Pilots, engagements, and press. Model optimization, edge deployment, benchmarking and model selection, and scoped on-premises pilots, plus press and partnership inquiries. labs@rogerai.fm Security disclosure. Report privately; please do not open a public issue. security@rogerai.fm · Policy Billing and accounts. billing@rogerai.fm · Privacy. privacy@rogerai.fm · Legal. legal@rogerai.fm The work itself. The source is public and the notebook is open. Reading either tells you more than a sales call would. Source · Open Air Waves

careers.html.text: (( • )) JOIN US Engineers for engineers. Operators for operators. RogerAI is an American AI research company in Orange County, California, building open models for hardware people actually own and the inference network that carries them. We are small and early, the work is published in the open as it happens, and the person who builds a thing here is the person who explains it. See open roles Read the research Read the source WHERE Orange County, California. Remote considered for the right person. STAGE Early and small. You will own a surface, not a ticket queue. Rolling = interviewing now; the work is continuous. §1 / RESEARCH Make the model small enough to matter. The Wave program builds models sized to the machine they live on, from single-machine task models up to workstation-class reasoning. Nothing ships until it passes its release gate on real devices. Edge model research Orange County or remote Full-time Rolling Own a slot in the Wave family end to end: architecture and tokenizer bake-offs against a fixed token budget, supervised fine-tuning, and the measurement that decides whether it ships at all. You will write the field note when the answer is no. Touches PyTorch, LoRA/full SFT, tokenizer design, eval harness construction, Hugging Face. Apply by email Quantization and compression Orange County or remote Full-time Rolling Take frontier-scale open models down to hardware people own without pretending the quality delta is zero. Pruning, low-precision execution, GGUF conversion, and the honest error bars that go with each. Touches llama.cpp, GGUF, MXFP4/Q4_K_M, expert pruning, CUDA and ROCm, perplexity and task-level evaluation. Apply by email §2 / ENGINEERING The radio, the desk, and everything under them. An OpenAI-compatible endpoint over machines we do not control, with capacity-aware routing, failover, metering and signed receipts - and a terminal client people actually enjoy using. Inference and runtime engineering Orange County or remote Full-time Rolling Serving throughput and context economics on real GPUs: batching, KV-cache behavior, speculative decoding, and the difference between a benchmark number and what a station sustains for an hour. Touches llama.cpp and vLLM internals, C++/CUDA, Go, OpenAI-compatible protocol surfaces. Apply by email Distributed systems engineering Orange County or remote Full-time Rolling The broker: discovery, routing, failover, metering and the signed receipt trail that makes payouts auditable. Multi-instance state that stays correct when a station drops mid-stream. Touches Go, Postgres, Valkey, Ed25519 receipts, Stripe Connect, testcontainers, exhaustive spec-first testing. Apply by email §3 / INDUSTRIAL DEPLOYMENT Where the data cannot leave the building. Plants, field sites and vehicles run segmented or air-gapped networks. That constraint is the whole opportunity, and it is not learned from a laptop. Industrial deployment engineering Orange County, with site travel Full-time Rolling Put local models to work beside existing control systems in oil and gas, power generation, manufacturing and aerospace - advisory only, never in a protection or safety path. Scope a pilot, measure it, and publish what it actually did. Touches OPC UA, Modbus, MQTT Sparkplug B and a unified namespace, ISA-95, NAMUR NE 107, IEC 62443 zoning, historians. Apply by email §4 / HOW TO APPLY Send work, not a cover letter. There is no applicant tracking system and no form. A person reads every message. What to include. Anything that shows how you think: a repository, a paper, a build log, a bug you chased to the bottom. One paragraph on what you would want to own here is worth more than a page of history. None of these fit? Send an open application anyway. Tell us what you are good at and what you would build, and if it is close to where we are going we will find the shape. careers@rogerai.fm What we will tell you. Whether it is a fit, and why not if it is not. We are too small to leave people waiting, and being ignored by a company that publishes its failures would be an odd start. What we cannot offer yet. We are early. Compensation is discussed honestly and individually rather than advertised as a band we have not set, and we will tell you plainly what the company is and is not before you decide anything. §5 / WHY HERE Built in America. Open to everyone. The models, the runtimes and the evidence are published as they are made, because a lab that only shows its wins is not doing science. If you want your work read, argued with, and run on somebody's Raspberry Pi in a plant in Ohio, that is the job.

faq.html.text: (( • )) ROGERAI · questions Asked often. Answered straight. All of this is in the manual somewhere, which is the problem: nobody reads a manual to find out whether a stranger can see their files. Short answers here, and a line under each one pointing at the place that says it in full. Where the honest answer is uncomfortable, it is the uncomfortable one. The manual → Pricing § / CONTENTS All of it, on one screen. §1 / GETTING STARTED Before you install anything. Do I need an account to use RogerAI? Not to browse, and not to use a free station. You can install the CLI, read the live directory of models, and open an endpoint against a station broadcasting at zero without signing in at all. You log in when you want a funded wallet to spend on paid stations, or when you want to earn as an operator. Manual · three commands, no account → What do I install, and on what? One binary called roger , on macOS, Linux or Windows. It is the same program for both sides of the network: the client that tunes in to somebody else's model and the server that puts yours on the air. There is nothing to run as a daemon and nothing to configure before the first run. Manual · install the set → Will it work with the tools I already use? Yes, if they speak the OpenAI API, which nearly everything does. Tuning in hands you a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint and key on 127.0.0.1 , so you change a base URL and a key in whatever you already run and nothing else. Editors, agents, SDKs and orchestration frameworks all work without a plugin. Field guide · connect your bots → Which models can I use? Whatever people have on the air at the moment you look, which is why the directory is live rather than a published list. Each model is a band and each machine serving it is a station on that band. The dial is the only honest answer to this question. The live dial → What happens if the station I am using goes off air? You get re-tuned to another station on the same band that still fits the limits you set, and your endpoint address does not change. Home machines get shut, rebooted and unplugged, so failover is the normal case here rather than an incident. You are never billed for an answer that did not arrive. Manual · lock a signal, get an endpoint → §2 / WHAT IT COSTS Money, and the guards around it. What does it cost to use a model? Whatever the operator set, per token, priced separately for input and output in dollars per million. Many stations charge nothing. We do not set, subsidize or floor the number, so there is no price list to publish - the current rate for any band is on the live dial. Pricing · the rules → Is there a subscription or a minimum? No. No plan, no seat, no monthly minimum, no annual commitment and nothing to cancel. You top up a wallet in whatever amount you want and it is debited per token as you spend it; if you stop sending requests you stop spending. Manual · one account, one wallet → Can a station charge me more than I agreed to? No. Your maximum price rides every single request rather than being checked once when you connect, so a station cannot raise its rate under you mid-session. If you set no limit at all the client still caps you at ten dollars per million output tokens, and accepting anything above twenty means typing the price back rather than pressing a key. Pricing · price safety → What if the answer comes back empty or unusable? It costs you nothing. A request that returns nothing usable is voided: the pre-authorized hold is released, you pay zero, the operator earns zero and takes a strike against their station. The rule is enforced at the broker, so it holds for any client, not only ours. Manual · fair billing → Can a station over-report how many tokens it served? Not profitably. The broker counts the tokens independently rather than trusting the station's claim, and settles on the smaller of the two figures. Both sides then sign a lineage receipt recording which node served which request, so the ledger can be audited afterwards by either of you. The Tower · metering and receipts → How do I add money, and who holds my card? Top-ups run through Stripe Checkout from the CLI or the billing page. Stripe is the payments provider and the regulated business that moves the funds, and it holds every card number and bank detail. We store a wallet balance and a ledger of top-ups and spend, and never see a card. Privacy · payments and payouts → §3 / SHARING YOUR GPU Putting a machine of yours on the air. How much do I keep of what I earn? Ninety percent of every token you serve, at a price you set yourself. The ten percent platform fee covers routing, metering, settlement, chargeback and fraud exposure, and the payout rails. When the work crosses a relay instead, the split is ninety to the serving node, five to the Tower operator, five to the platform. Pricing · what you earn → When do I actually get paid? Earnings accrue immediately; the principal (90%) is held 30 days and a 10% reserve slice stays back until day 90 to cover the late-chargeback tail before they become payable. After that you request a payout and payable balances are released on a monthly batch, with a minimum of $25. Stripe Connect onboarding has to be complete first, and Stripe rather than RogerAI holds your identity documents. Manual · earnings and payouts → Do I have to open a port or set up a static IP? No, and this is the point of the design. Your machine opens an outbound connection to the tower and pulls work down it; nothing is ever pushed in at you. There is no inbound port to forward, no dynamic DNS to keep current, and nothing new exposed on your home network. The Tower · who does the dialing → What can the person using my GPU reach on my machine? The model endpoint, and nothing else. RogerAI bridges the port your inference server is already listening on. It does not offer a shell, a filesystem, your other services or the rest of your network, and a request that tries to reach anything but the model is refused before it leaves the tower. Security · our posture → Can I serve for free, or only for money? Free is the default and a lot of the band runs that way. A station with a rate of zero is a normal station: it is listed, routed to and scored exactly like a paid one, and it is not throttled into uselessness to push you toward charging. You can also mix the two, with free hours and paid hours on a schedule. Manual · put your GPU on the air → Why did my earnings stop? Usually a hold rather than a ban, and usually a bug rather than bad faith: the broker caught your node's own signed numbers contradicting each other, which a misconfigured station does on every request. Run roger drphil and it will tell you which. A hold lifts by itself after seven days, and the evidence behind every strike is yours to read. Manual · when the signal drops → Can I resell my provider contract as a station? Yes. Put the contract on the air as a curated station - one flag, roger share --curated , plus the list price you already pay. Consumers pay that list plus a 10% routing fee; you get your bill back in full and keep half the fee, so the math can never go against you. The band wears the curated mark and every receipt shows the split. Verification costs you one canary at sign-up and a small weekly recheck, usually under a cent a month. Pricing · every way in → §4 / PRIVACY AND SAFETY The part worth reading before you send anything real. Can the operator read my prompts? On an ordinary station, treat the answer as yes. The operator's machine runs the model, which means the text is in that machine's memory while it is being answered, exactly as it is with any hosted endpoint anywhere. If that is not acceptable for your work, the confidential tier routes only to nodes that pass hardware attestation, where the memory holding your request is encrypted against the host itself. The confidential tier → Does a model provider know who I am? No. Whoever serves your request sees a station making calls - not your account, your card, or your IP, because stations dial out and nothing ever connects back to you. One thing we won't pretend: the words themselves still reach the machine that answers them. When even that is too much, use a confidential station or run your own Tower. Why route through us · the whole argument → Do you keep my prompts? No. For a settled request we persist token counts, cost and hashes in the signed receipt, not your text, and we never train on it. There is one transient exception and one legal one: prompts we relay are screened in transit against a moderation model before dispatch, and apparent child sexual abuse material is preserved and reported because United States law requires it. Privacy · prompt content and the safety screen → What is the confidential tier? A subset of the network that only accepts nodes proving, through real hardware attestation, that they are running inside a trusted execution environment. On that path the machine's owner cannot read the request out of memory while it is being served. It needs data-center silicon, so it is a smaller band than the open one rather than a setting you switch on. What it is, and what it needs → What if a station misbehaves? Report it from the control on that station in the model directory, or by mail to abuse. Strikes accumulate against a station's record and follow it, and a ban needs several of them corroborated by more than one kind of signal rather than one angry report. A station that cannot answer is already earning nothing, because unusable answers are voided. Security · report abuse or a station → §5 / NOT ANSWERED HERE Ask, and it probably ends up on this page. The manual is the long form and the source is the longest form of all. If neither settles it, a few lines to a real mailbox will. Let’s talk Every command Source

security.html.text: Security How the platform is built to fail safe, and how to report a problem. Our posture Nodes reach the broker over an outbound-only tunnel - an operator's machine opens the connection out, so there are no inbound ports to expose on a home network. Work is pulled, never pushed in. Every settled request carries an Ed25519-signed lineage receipt , so which node served which request can be verified and cannot be forged. The browser talks to the broker over credentialed CORS against an allow-listed origin; the session lives in a signed, http-only cookie and no access tokens ever touch page JavaScript. Stripe holds all PCI card data and all KYC identity documents. We never store card numbers, bank details, or identity documents on our side. Report a vulnerability Please report security issues privately - do not open a public issue or PR. Preferred: GitHub private vulnerability reporting on the repo ( Security → Report a vulnerability ). Or email security@rogerai.fm . We aim to acknowledge within 72 hours. Please include reproduction steps and impact; we will coordinate a fix and a disclosure timeline with you. Full policy: SECURITY.md . Machine-readable contact: /.well-known/security.txt (RFC 9116). Report abuse or a station For abuse, prohibited content, or a misbehaving station - not a software vulnerability - use the report control on each station in the Models directory, or email abuse@rogerai.fm . The Acceptable Use Policy is in the Terms . We act on reports, and a station's record follows it. Privacy - Terms - Report abuse - Account

privacy.html.text: Privacy What we collect, why, and how to get it out or wipe it. Written plainly. Who we are RogerAI is RogerAI, Inc., a Delaware corporation operating from Orange County, California - the platform behind rogerai.fm and the broker at broker.rogerai.fm. It routes prompts to self-hosted nodes and settles pay-per-token between consumers and node operators. This page covers the data the platform itself handles. Stripe (our payments provider) and our sign-in providers - GitHub, Apple, and the service that mails your sign-in code - handle data under their own policies, linked below. Groq (our moderation provider) also processes prompt text for a transient safety screen, described under "Prompt content and the safety screen". Account and identity There are three ways to sign in, and each leaves a different amount behind. We never receive or store a password for any of them. GitHub. We receive and store your numeric GitHub user id, your login (handle), and your display name if you have set one. Only if you choose to save one do we store a contact email. Your avatar is never copied or hosted by us - the page loads it straight from GitHub's public avatar CDN by your numeric id, and only for accounts that have a GitHub handle. Apple. Sign in with Apple gives us one identifier: the app-scoped sub Apple issues for RogerAI. It is not your Apple ID, and it is specific to us. If you let Apple share an address we store it as your contact email - including Apple's private relay address, if that is the one you chose. Apple sends your name only on the very first sign-in; we keep it to address the welcome email. Apple accounts have no avatar and nothing is loaded from Apple. Email. We mail a short code to the address you type and you send it back. While a code is outstanding we store hashes only - one of the address, one of the code - never the code itself, and the record expires ten minutes after it is issued. We also count recent requests per address and per sender, to stop our mailer being used to flood someone's inbox. Once you complete the round trip we record the address and the moment it was verified. A verified address is an identity; an address you merely typed into your profile is not, and we never resolve a sign-in against one. One account can carry more than one of these. Linking GitHub and Apple on the same device key, or verifying an address a provider already gave us, joins them into a single account with a single wallet rather than quietly creating a second. Payments and payouts Stripe is the payments provider and the regulated money services business that moves the funds. Top-ups run through Stripe Checkout and operator payouts through Stripe Connect after the payout hold (30 days, with a 10% reserve to day 90) and Stripe KYC. We never see, store, or process your card number, bank details, or KYC identity documents - Stripe holds all of that. On our side we keep only a wallet balance, a ledger of top-ups and spend, accrued earnings (your 90% share after the 10% platform fee), and the Stripe account/reference ids needed to reconcile a payment. For operators, tax and reporting obligations (for example a US Form 1099) may require Stripe and/or us to collect tax information and report earnings to the relevant tax authority; the money, fee, and tax terms are in the Terms . Usage and lineage When you send a request we record what is needed to bill it and to settle the operator: the model or node used, token counts, cost, and a timestamp. Settled requests produce a lineage receipt - a signed record of which node served which request - so both sides can audit the ledger. We do not sell your data or use prompt contents to train models. Prompt content and the safety screen The broker is content-blind for the marketplace. For a settled request it persists only token counts, cost, and hashes in the signed receipt - it does not store or read your prompt or the response text, and it never uses them to train models. The one honest exception is a transient, pre-dispatch safety screen , and it covers requests the broker relays : before such a prompt is passed to a node, its text is checked against a moderation model so we can refuse content we do not allow on the network (see the Terms and the Acceptable Use Policy). That screen runs in transit - the prompt is not stored for it - but it does mean the text is read by the screen at dispatch time, and is sent to Groq (below), our moderation provider, as a third party for that check. Traffic that goes through a relay is not pre-screened. There is a second way a request can reach a node: straight from you to the node through a relay (a "Tower"), which may be ours or another operator's. On that path the broker never receives your prompt - it issues an authorization naming a model and some limits, and the prompt and the answer travel around it, encrypted end to end to the node that serves you. That is better for confidentiality, and the trade is worth saying plainly: there is nothing for the safety screen to read, so nothing is screened before dispatch. Policy enforcement on that path happens afterwards, on a sample , from signed transcripts the serving node keeps. So content we do not allow can be served on that path and only found later. Any signed-in node can serve this way, so treat it as a live path rather than an exotic one. The one mandatory exception: child sexual abuse material (CSAM). If the safety screen flags a prompt as apparent CSAM, US law (18 USC 2258A) requires us to preserve the offending request and report it to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). In that single case the flagged request is preserved encrypted and access-controlled for a limited period, under a pseudonym, solely to meet that legal obligation and to distinguish repeat offenders. This is the only situation in which we retain prompt content, and we have zero tolerance for CSAM (see the Acceptable Use Policy in the Terms). Ping, the on-site concierge. The little chat assistant on the website answers questions about RogerAI. It first tries a free on-air community station; if none is available it falls back to Groq . So a message you type into Ping may be sent to a community node or to Groq to produce a reply. Do not put secrets into Ping - it is a public, unauthenticated demo surface, not a private channel. Remote control (Base Station) When you run /remote-control in the roger agent, that live session becomes continuable from your other signed-in surfaces (another terminal, the web Base Station, the app). It is private to your account : only you, signed into the same account, can see or join it, and a short-lived one-time code is required to link a device that is not already logged in. What the broker relays, and what it does not keep. While a session is on the air, the broker relays the session's messages, tool names, and confirmations between your surfaces so a second screen can follow along. Those frames pass through the broker in transit only - they are held in a small, bounded, in-memory buffer to bridge a brief reconnect and are never written to disk or to our database . The broker stores only the session's metadata (a name, creation time, token hashes , and revocation state), never the transcript. The conversation itself lives on the host machine that is running the agent. Honest about the security model. The relay is carried over TLS to the broker, but it is not end-to-end encrypted : because the broker forwards the frames, their text is readable at the relay in transit (it is not retained). Tools always run on the host machine, and only after a confirmation. End the session any time with /remote-control off or from Base Station; revoking it drops the buffer and invalidates every link and device token immediately. Deleting your account revokes all remote-control sessions. Cookies We use a single cookie: a signed, http-only session cookie set by the broker after you log in. It is not readable by JavaScript and no access tokens are ever exposed to the page. We do not use advertising or third-party tracking cookies. Your browser may send GitHub's own cookies when loading a GitHub avatar from GitHub's CDN; that is GitHub's cookie, not ours, and it does not happen at all on an Apple or email account. What we log Operationally we keep request and billing records (above), plus standard server logs needed to run and secure the service - for example error traces and abuse/fraud signals. We retain de-identified financial records for the legal retention window (tax and anti-money-laundering rules - typically up to 7 years) even after an account is deleted. Your data: export and delete You control your data from the Account page. Export. "Export my data" calls POST /account/export and downloads a JSON copy of the account data we hold for you. Delete. "Delete account" calls POST /account/delete . Every identifier that could name you or sign you back in is cleared: your GitHub id and handle, your Apple sub , your name, and your email address. The handle is replaced with an opaque marker so it can never be resolved again, and no sign-in route - GitHub, Apple, or email - can reach the account afterwards. What remains are de-identified financial records, keyed only by the account's public key, kept for the legal window described above. The action cannot be undone, and it is refused while you still hold a balance, unswept earnings, or an open dispute - settle those first. One honest limit while we finish the work: the delete route is keyed to your account handle, so an account created with Apple alone - one that never linked a GitHub handle - cannot yet complete it by itself. If that is you, mail privacy@rogerai.fm and we will do it for you. We would rather say so here than let the button imply otherwise. Third parties The processors we rely on: GitHub (sign-in and avatars), Apple (Sign in with Apple), Resend (delivering sign-in codes and account notices), Stripe (payments, payouts, KYC), Groq (the pre-dispatch safety screen described above, and Ping's fallback - prompt text is sent to Groq for those checks and replies), and our hosting provider (serving the site and broker). Each handles your data under its own privacy policy. Contact Questions, an export problem, or a data request: email privacy@rogerai.fm . For security issues see the Security page. To report abuse or a station, email abuse@rogerai.fm or use the report control on the Models directory. Account - Terms - Security

tos.html.text: Read this These Terms are written plainly and are a real, binding agreement when you use RogerAI. The service, the site, and all model output are provided "as is" with no warranty, and your use is at your own risk - the detail is in sections 2 and 3. Nothing here is legal advice and these Terms are not a substitute for advice from your own lawyer. If you have legal questions about your own use, consult your own counsel. Terms of Service and Acceptable Use The agreement between you and RogerAI ("we", "us"). By using the site, the CLI, the broker, or by going on air as an operator, you accept these Terms. If you do not agree, do not use the service. Last updated 2026-09 (the operating entity is now RogerAI, Inc., a Delaware corporation). Money, payout, dispute, and refund terms are in sections 7 to 10; metering, billing-integrity, and anti-abuse terms are in section 11. 1. What RogerAI is RogerAI is a marketplace and relay. It helps consumers discover self-hosted, third-party "node" operators running large language models on their own hardware, and it settles pay-per-token between the two sides. We do not run the models that serve your requests, and we do not produce the output. Node operators are independent third parties, not our employees or agents. We relay requests and responses, meter usage, and settle payment; we do not control what a node returns. Towers. Some requests reach a node through an independent third-party Tower - a relay operator who provides network reach and bandwidth so a node need not connect to us directly. A Tower cannot read the content it relays. When your request is served through a Tower, it is billed to your wallet exactly like any other request (section 7), and the Tower operator earns a share of the request for the traffic they carried, paid out of RogerAI's platform fee (section 8). Tower-relayed inference requires a signed-in account - see section 7. 2. Output is provided "as is" - no warranty This is important because we relay third-party output. The service, the site, the CLI, the broker, and all model output are provided "as is" and "as available", without warranties of any kind , whether express, implied, or statutory - including the implied warranties of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, accuracy, and non-infringement. We do not warrant that output is correct, complete, current, safe, lawful, or fit for any purpose. Model output can be wrong, biased, or harmful.
